title: Redwood Console: Tracing & Request Logs Walkthrough
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Customer owns an on-prem inference stack currently and is evaluating Redwood for lower latency/cost and better debugging. Discussed hosted vs dedicated, VPC and SOC2 questions, and next steps to run a short pilot and share security docs.
next_steps: Ava to send Dedicated pricing + pilot terms (by 2027-02-25)
Matt to run a sample trace and share steps + screenshots (by 2027-02-22)
Ethan to share a failing request-id and logs (by 2027-02-21)
Security team to receive SOC2 + network diagrams link (Ava)
Schedule follow-up bench run w/ 1k reqs (tentative week of 2027-03-01)

header:
Date: 2027-02-20
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Ava Sullivan (Redwood AE), Matt Rivers (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Acme CTO), Ethan Brooks (Lead ML Eng), Samira Khan (DevOps), Jules Kim (Redwood Product)
transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 45 minutes today, we'll run through the Console tracing and then jump into request logs and some debugging flows. Introductions quick?
[00:12] Priya (Acme): Hi, Priya here, CTO, we own infra and inference stack, currently on-prem with a mix of spare GPUs.
[00:18] Ethan (Acme): Ethan, ML eng, I'm usually digging into latency and model failures.
[00:22] Samira (Acme): Samira, DevOps, I handle network and infra.
[00:25] Ava: Great, and on our side Matt's gonna drive the demo.
[00:28] Matt (Redwood SE): Yep, hey all. Ok first slide — um, opening the console, you can see tracing for live requests, we surface per-request timelines and spans, and we tie that to request-ids so you can jump to raw logs.
[00:40] Matt: So here's a trace — you can expand the token generation span, see kernel-level durations, and see if the stall was on KV cache lookup or on the compilation step.
[00:52] Priya: Sorry, when you say KV cache, is that on our side or Redwood's?
[00:56] Matt: Good question. For hosted we maintain the prefix cache; for Dedicated we can either run cache co-located on your GPU nodes or use a sharded cache architecture, you can control retention.
[01:08] Samira: And for Private / VPC we need to make sure that cache traffic stays inside the VPC, right?
[01:12] Ava: Yes, for VPC/on-prem variants traffic never leaves your network. We also support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
[01:20] Ethan: Walk me through a typical error flow — we often see generation truncation and occasionally OOMs. How do we find root cause?
[01:27] Matt: So two things: trace will show per-span memory signals and we attach request logs with token counts and sequence length. Example here, you can see request 0x9a3f — sequence length spiked at 6k which pushed us into a different kernel path and caused the slow down.
[01:41] Priya: Are those request-ids something we can map to our logs?
[01:44] Matt: Yes, you can inject your correlation-id in the API call, and it shows up in the request logs. We also preserve original headers for compliance where permitted.
[01:52] Ava: I also wanted to touch on error analysis — the console highlights deviations in output quality, and you can attach a sample prompt set to monitor regressions.
[02:10] Ethan: How accurate is the auto-classification of errors? We need to reduce noise; our SCM generates a lot of transient failures.
[02:16] Matt: It's heuristic-based today, we flag timeouts, OOMs, auth errors separately. You can filter by error type and then deep-dive with traces. It's not perfect, sometimes it mislabels a bad prompt as a model error but you can tag and correct it.
[02:30] Samira: From a network/security perspective, we need SOC 2 docs and diagram of egress points. Who do we send that to?
[02:35] Ava: I'll send the SOC 2 report and network diagram; for Dedicated we can provide diagrams showing no egress for VPC setups.
[02:42] Priya: Ok good. Cost question — does tracing add cost or latency when enabled?
[02:46] Matt: Tracing is sampled by default; turning on full traces adds a small CPU overhead for metadata collection but we stream logs to storage asynchronously. For Dedicated you can turn off collection or adjust sampling rates; it's a tradeoff of observability vs overhead.
[02:59] Ethan: We're also evaluating Anthropic / OpenAI; their tooling is less tailored to dedicated infra. Any guidance on migration?
[03:08] Ava: We typically help with a short pilot — you run a week of traces on your critical routes; we run side-by-side throughput and latency comparisons. For quantization and batching config, Redwood Optimize can suggest safe quantization with minimal quality loss.
[03:22] Matt: Demoing the request logs — you can search by model, route, request-id, time window. Here's an example of a failing request: status 500 with model-side error, stack shows tokenization failing due to malformed utf-8 in the prompt.
[03:36] Samira: Would that be an integration issue? We sanitize inputs but sometimes legacy data slips in.
[03:40] Matt: Yeah likely integration; the logs show the raw prompt and the tokenizer exception. We also surface a backtrace and the kernel that errored, which helps SEs reproduce.
[03:52] Priya: For pilot scope — we want to test: (1) latency under 50ms p50 for our typical prompts, (2) error debugability (we want to see if we can reproduce a truncation bug), (3) security requirements: VPC and KMS. Is that reasonable?
[04:05] Ava: Totally. Typical pilot runs are 1-2 weeks with a small traffic split. We'll provide a bench spreadsheet — we map your p50/p95 and cost per token across model variants.
[04:18] Ethan: On the truncation bug, can you show how to replay a request?
[04:22] Matt: Sure — in the trace you can click 'replay' which replay-sends the prompt to a replay environment; note we scrub PII unless configured otherwise. Replays can be run against older model versions too to check regressions.
[04:35] Samira: About SSO — we use SAML, ok to integrate?
[04:36] Ava: Yes SAML/SSO supported, RBAC with SCIM provisioning. We'll include setup docs.
[04:42] Priya: Any hard limits on retention for request logs? We need at least 90 days for audit.
[04:47] Matt: Hosted default is 30 days in standard plan; Dedicated/Private you can configure retention, and longer retention is an add-on. We can support 90+ days with an enterprise plan.
[05:00] Ethan: Can we see an example timeline where a fallback occurred? We sometimes see our app hit a fallback to a cheaper model and outputs change.
[05:07] Matt: Yep here's an example — routing policy had a cost threshold, requests were routed to a 7B variant and you can see the quality delta in the error analysis tab and the model-version at the time.
[05:20] Ava: Quick question for Priya — timeline for procurement?
[05:23] Priya: We're targeting a vendor decision in 6 weeks, budget sign-off by end of quarter.
[05:28] Ava: Ok that aligns — next steps we'll share pricing and a pilot SOW.
[05:34] Matt: I'll follow up with concrete steps to reproduce the truncation — could you send us the sample request-id?
[05:38] Ethan: Yes I'll send 0x9a3f and the correlated logs after this call.
[05:42] Samira: And I'll loop in our network team — need to check firewall rules for VPC peering.
[05:45] Ava: Great. Any other questions before we close?
[05:49] Priya: One last — encryption keys, HSM support?
[05:52] Jules (Redwood Product): We support customer-managed keys in KMS and HSM integrations on Private deployments; we'll surface the doc.
[05:58] Ava: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the documents and schedule the bench.
[06:02] END: Call wraps up, a few folks linger for 1:1s.
